requirements.text: log an incident for this hardware issue and route it to the onsite hardware technicians; the highest level of urgency due to high impact
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_011' AND short_description LIKE '%Bitlocker%' AND description LIKE '%client site%' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND category = 'hardware' AND assignment_group = 'GROUP_005' AND channel = 'phone' AND status = 'new' AND assigned_to IS NULL AND service IS NULL AND service_offering IS NULL AND configuration_item IS NULL AND worknotes IS NULL AND resolution_notes IS NULL AND close_notes IS NULL AND resolution_code IS NULL AND on_hold_reason IS NULL AND parent_incident IS NULL AND problem IS NULL AND change_request IS NULL AND caused_by_change IS NULL AND resolved_by IS NULL AND incident_template IS NULL AND resolved IS NULL
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100); the only incident the task creates
Travis Wood = USER_011 (travis.wood@servicenow.com, active agent, ORG_001), the only Travis or Wood in users; caller_id is the user affected (policy 3.1)
'the highest level of urgency due to high impact' read as urgency high and impact high; priority critical from the policy matrix
category hardware from 'this hardware issue'; the seed uses the value 'hardware'

'onsite hardware technicians' read as GROUP_005 L1 Field Support (type Field Support Technicians, description 'Basic On-site Repairs and Installs'), as the benchmark check tests; GROUP_006 L2 Field Support ('Complex Hardware Diagnostics') is the other Field Support group, but a recovery-screen unlock is a basic on-site repair and 'onsite' matches GROUP_005's description
channel phone from 'just called'; this policy sets no channel default
status new from the policy default for new incidents (3.1)

short_description LIKE '%Bitlocker%' and description LIKE '%client site%' kept from the benchmark check; the request gives the words but not the exact text (SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive, so 'BitLocker' also matches)
assigned_to IS NULL kept from the benchmark check: the request routes to a group, names no person, and the policy says not to assume optional arguments
configuration_item IS NULL kept from the benchmark check: the request names no device and no listed tool looks up a CI, although the seed holds CI_027 (MacBook Pro 14 - Travis Wood)

the remaining IS NULL cells (service, service_offering, worknotes, resolution and closure fields, links) kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, and nothing in the request asks to set them

also carries the incident part of cross_table_integrity_verification (incident INC_101, caller USER_011, group GROUP_005, priority critical, status new, category hardware); its joined user, group and article facts hold on the seed and no listed tool writes those tables

requirements.text: find and link the Bitlocker recovery procedure article to the ticket
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_kb_id = 'IKB_046' AND incident_id = 'INC_101' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_012' AND used_as = 'suggested'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (IKB_046 after IKB_045); the only link the task creates, so the row is anchored by id
KB_012 'Bitlocker Recovery Key' ('Laptop Encryption', published, ORG_001) is the only Bitlocker or recovery article in title, short description or body
used_as suggested from policy 7 (articles matched when an incident is created are linked as suggested); the request names no use type
incident_id INC_101 as assumed in the incident requirement
also carries the link part of cross_table_integrity_verification (a KB_012 link on INC_101 with used_as suggested)

cross_table_integrity_verification.evidence: a join conjunction of the two checks above with a subset of their cells (incident INC_101 critical, new, hardware, caller USER_011, group GROUP_005; a KB_012 link used_as suggested), carried jointly by the incident and link requirements, which name it in their source; its other joined cells (USER_011 active, GROUP_005 active with type Field Support Technicians, KB_012 published) are seed facts no listed tool can change

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement, cell and value (incident INC_101 for USER_011, high/high/critical, hardware, GROUP_005, phone, new, the benchmark's null cells; link IKB_046 to KB_012 as suggested) and on all three dispositions (kept); no disagreement between them is left to resolve.
Both passes carried the cross-table join check as a third requirement restating the other two; it is carried jointly instead, named in the source of the incident and link requirements, because a conjunction of cells that other carried checks already test is not a separate thing the request asks, and its remaining joined cells are seed facts.
The acting user USER_004 (Joanne Simpson, manager, ORG_001) may create incidents under the policy. Two judgement calls a reviewer may weigh: GROUP_005 (L1) versus GROUP_006 (L2) for 'onsite hardware technicians' (both are Field Support Technicians; GROUP_005's description says 'On-site', so the benchmark's choice is kept), and configuration_item IS NULL although Travis Wood owns CI_027 in the seed (no CI lookup tool is listed and the request names no device, so the benchmark's null is kept). No stay requirements: the incident and link are anchored by id and only one article matches, so there is no selector boundary to guard.
